Rudder pressure maintained after the turn is established will cause the airplane to skid to the I outside of the turn. If a definite effort is made to center the rudder rather than let it streamline itself to the turn, it is probable that some opposite rudder pressure will be exerted inadvertently. This will force the airplane to yaw opposite its turning path, causing the airplane to slip to the inside of the turn. The ball in the turn-and- slip indicator will be displaced off-center whenever the airplane is skidding or slipping sideways.
